newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's Hiscox Select trims 1997 capacity.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's Hiscox Select trims 1997 capacity.

text.p: Hiscox Select Insurance Fund Plc, one of the corporate investors in Lloyds of London, said on Thursday it is reducing its underwriting capacity for 1997 to 57.79 million from 58.77 million stg.
"As indicated in the half yearly statement we have reduced our exposure in the marine market where conditions are the most competitive," the company said in a statement.
Lloyd's has capacity -- the amount of premium income it can write -- of around 10 billion stg this year. Figures on the amount of capacity available to the market next year are expected next week.
Capacity is based on the amount investors, both individuals, known as Names, and corporate backers, are willing to subscribe to the market each year.

Hiscox Select said it has also reduced the number of underwriting syndicates in its fund to 36 from 56, partly due to the merger of some managing agents. Some 160 syndicates are operating in Lloyd's this year.
The company has allocated 21 percent of its capacity to the three syndicates managed by managing agent Hiscox Syndicates Ltd compared with 23 percent for the 1996 underwriting year.
"This reduction has been caused by all three syndicates reducing their capacity to all capital providers to help them to match their capacity with their estimated premium income," the statement said.

Hiscox added that it had been active in this year's capacity auctions -- run by Lloyd's for investors to buy and sell their rights in the market -- and had further concentrated its capacity on its core syndicates.

Commenting on the market outlook for 1997, Hiscox Select said rates continued to soften, "although we remain confident that the quality and composition of the 1997 portfolio is well positioned to weather these difficult underwriting conditions and produce satisfactory underwriting profits."
